name: John Markus Lervik
current_role: Founder, Cognite (Oslo industrial data/AI software); CEO until April 2022, then Chief Strategy & Development Officer
profile: Norwegian tech entrepreneur (b. 1969) with an NTNU PhD. He was CEO of Fast Search & Transfer until Microsoft bought it in 2008, founded ad/analytics firm Cxense in 2010, and in 2016 co-founded Cognite, the Aker-backed industrial DataOps company described as Norway's first unicorn. Girish Rishi took over as CEO in 2022; Cognite now lists Lervik as Founder.
interesting_fact: When he handed over the CEO role in 2022, Cognite's announcement credited him with building Cognite into 'Norway's first unicorn'.
deep_cut_fact: He was the first person hired at Fast Search & Transfer, and he won an Esso academic award for his NTNU PhD work in 1996. He is a fellow of the Norwegian Academy of Technological Sciences.

public_contacts.value: michelle.holford@cognite.com (Michelle Holford, Global PR Lead, Cognite)

notes: Strong fit for the energy/data angle: Cognite does industrial data for oil and gas and utilities. Avoid the 2014 FAST accounting conviction. Cognite now lists him only as 'Founder', so his day-to-day role may be smaller. The PR email was in the media-contact box on a Cognite newsroom page.

name: Pablo Zamora
current_role: President of the board, Fundación Chile (since 2022, proposed by President Boric). Co-founder and former CSO of NotCo. Investor and board member.
profile: Chilean biochemist with a PhD in biotechnology from Universidad de Santiago. In 2015 he co-founded NotCo, the AI-driven plant-based food company later valued as a unicorn, with Matías Muchnick and Karim Pichara. He was CSO from 2018 to March 2020, then left to work as an investor and consultant. He chairs Fundación Chile, whose board is split between the Chilean state and BHP, and was named to BancoEstado's board.
interesting_fact: Fundación Chile's board, which he chairs, is half appointed by the Chilean state and half by the mining company BHP. That gives him a seat where mining, energy and innovation policy meet.
deep_cut_fact: Before NotCo he did postdoctoral research on the genetics of Mexican maize at UC Davis from 2009. He also worked on plant and microbe genomics as a senior scientist with the Mars Advanced Research Institute (2013-2015).
notes: Spanish-language media covers him often (DF, El Mercurio). A 2026 DF piece hinted his Fundación Chile tenure may end with the change of government; I could not confirm his current status. He has spoken publicly about lithium (the SQM-Codelco deal), which fits an energy podcast. No personal email found.

name: Alexander Kent-Braham
current_role: Co-founder of Marshmallow (London car-insurance insurtech); per 2021 coverage he leads internal culture and product while his twin Oliver handles external matters
profile: British entrepreneur from south-west London who co-founded Marshmallow with his identical twin Oliver and engineer David Goaté. Marshmallow is a licensed UK car insurer that uses data to price cover for people traditional insurers turn away, such as recent migrants and drivers with thin credit files. It became a unicorn in 2021 with an $85M Series B at a $1.25B valuation.
interesting_fact: Marshmallow was only the second UK start-up with Black founders to be valued at more than $1 billion, after WorldRemit.
deep_cut_fact: Marshmallow was first incorporated in 2016 under the name 'Twin Thinking'. For its first 10 months the team worked from the lobby of a Virgin Active gym on an £80 membership ('a desk plus a sauna and a steam room').
notes: His twin Oliver is the usual press voice, so Alexander gives few interviews. I found no published press email for Marshmallow; the gym anecdote is quoted from Oliver in the Evening Standard (syndicated on Yahoo). I could not verify his current title.

name: Aaron Passey
current_role: Co-founder & Chief Architect, Qumulo (Seattle scale-out file-data platform)
profile: Caltech-trained systems engineer and Isilon Systems veteran who co-founded Qumulo in 2012 with Peter Godman and Neal Fachan and served as its first CTO. He stepped away in 2016, then returned in December 2022 as a senior principal engineer. Qumulo now lists him as Co-founder & Chief Architect; the company sells file storage for AI/GPU, energy and HPC workloads.
interesting_fact: Qumulo's three founders met at Isilon Systems. Passey left Qumulo in 2016 and rejoined in 2022, calling his return 'a true homecoming'.
deep_cut_fact: When he rejoined, Qumulo's CTO Kiran Bhageshpur noted that Passey had worked on four distinct distributed storage products and called him 'a fearless and imaginative technical leader'.
notes: A deeply technical engineer-founder with a low media profile. Good fit for a data-center storage conversation. The best route is Qumulo PR or LinkedIn (linked from Qumulo's leadership page).

name: Amir Jerbi
current_role: Co-founder of Aqua Security; strategic advisor since stepping down as CTO in November 2025
profile: Israeli security engineer who served about four years in an IDF IT unit and later became a chief architect at a large security software company (CA Technologies). In 2015 he co-founded Aqua Security with Dror Davidoff; the cloud-native and container security company reached a $1B valuation in 2021. In November 2025 both founders stepped back to advisory roles, Mike Dube became CEO and Nir Makowski became chief product and technology officer.
interesting_fact: Aqua grew out of a weekly meetup. Jerbi saw an early Docker demo, went home, 'fell in love' with containers within days, and then quit his chief-architect job to work on container security full time.
deep_cut_fact: He has said he decided that 'leveraging containers for better security was my destiny'. He first worked on it as a 'new hobby' before founding Aqua with friends a year later; the original idea was to make containerised apps 'secured anywhere' as well as 'run anywhere'.
notes: The leadership change is dated 5 Nov 2025 (Calcalist). As of 2025, Aqua's press releases appear to route media through an agency (Look Left Marketing), but I could not open the release to verify the address, so it is not recorded. Note that Aqua cut staff after the 2025 reorganisation. He is a technical voice on cloud and container security and appeared on 'The IaC Podcast'.

name: Vu Tran
current_role: Co-founder, Black Sky Industries (Logan, Qld solid-rocket-motor and defence manufacturer); co-founder and former Chief Growth Officer of Go1
profile: Dr Vu Tran is a Brisbane GP who grew up in Logan as a migrant. He co-founded workplace e-learning marketplace Go1 with school friends Andrew Barnes, Chris Eigeland and Chris Hood; Go1 raised $272M in 2021 and was valued at about $3B when it bought Blinkist in 2023. He has since stepped back from Go1's day-to-day running and co-founded Black Sky Industries, which makes solid rocket propellant and rocket motors for Australian defence.
interesting_fact: Black Sky Industries describes itself as Australia's only sovereign supplier of solid rocket propellant and motors, and it produces ammonium perchlorate locally. Tran argues Australia has only one local firm in the top 100 defence suppliers.
deep_cut_fact: In high school, instead of stacking shelves at Coles, he and Andrew Barnes started a software business that 'made a dollar an hour'. Around 2006 it was building websites for ANZ and News Corp, which did not realise they were dealing with students. He did not pay off his last credit-card debts until early 2020.

public_contacts.value: Long-form interview: 'Meet the Founder - Vu Tran (Go1)', The Exchange by EW Private Wealth, Sept 2024

notes: Practising GP (MBBS Bond, per profiles). Speaks readily on podcasts about sovereign manufacturing and defence, which suits an energy and industry angle. Also a non-executive director of ASX-listed PeopleIN (per marketindex; not re-verified). Black Sky's site has only a contact section, no published email.

name: Justin Waldron
current_role: Co-founder and President, Playco (Tokyo instant-play web games company), per 2020 coverage; current title not re-confirmed
profile: American game developer and angel investor who co-founded Zynga at 19 and was lead engineer/designer on its first game, Texas Hold'em Poker (later Zynga Poker). He rose to SVP Product before leaving in October 2013. He then co-founded Playco in Tokyo with Game Closure's Michael Carter; it raised a $100M Series A in September 2020 at just over $1B, making it a unicorn.
interesting_fact: He was only 19 when he built Zynga Poker, Zynga's first game. On leaving in 2013 he wrote that it had been 'six and a half years since we pushed the button to launch our first game, and each moment since has been magic'.
deep_cut_fact: Before Playco he had invested in more than 50 startups, including Snackpass and Substack. He relocated to Tokyo to run Playco as President.

public_contacts.value: Colossus episode 'Waldron: The Future of Social Gaming'

notes: Lower profile than Zynga co-founder Mark Pincus. Playco's site is still live (games: Everwing, Heads Up!, Buruburu Do Butsu), but I found no post-2021 news on the company's status or his current title. The Colossus podcast page blocked automated access, so I confirmed it only from search results. Several sources say he dropped out of UConn to co-found Zynga.

name: Yu Qianli
current_role: Co-founder, Xiaoe-tech (小鹅通, Shenzhen private-domain operations / creator-commerce SaaS)
profile: One of the ex-Tencent co-founders of Xiaoe-tech, the Shenzhen SaaS company led by founder-CEO Bao Chunjian (鲍春健). Its tools help merchants, educators and creators run e-commerce, marketing and CRM in their own channels. Investors include Tencent, Hillhouse, IDG and Qiming. Its 2021 Series D valued it at about HK$5.1B. It filed for a Hong Kong IPO in August 2025, and 36Kr reported a new attempt in May 2026.
interesting_fact: Xiaoe-tech's whole founding team came from Tencent. Founder Bao Chunjian left as a rare T4-level expert engineer with ¥5M of savings and burned through it in seven months before the business took off.
deep_cut_fact: 36Kr reports that this co-founder was previously responsible for product development on Tencent's QQ Zone (QQ空间). The article spells the name 喻干里, likely a misprint of 喻千里 (Yu Qianli).
notes: Very low public profile. The only mention I found is in 36Kr, which spells the name 喻干里 rather than 喻千里, so identity is marked uncertain until checked against the HKEX prospectus. Bao Chunjian is the public face and controlling shareholder (about 44.9% pre-IPO). Chinese-language outreach via the company's public-affairs email is the best route.
